lens: Could a fresh agent run this verify step in isolation and tell me unambiguously whether it passed?

findings.title: Target skill `eval:` field does not exercise the new `sprint-bucket` field — eval coverage gap
findings.claim: The mandatory eval-coverage check fails. `plugins/specflow/skills/task/SKILL.md` line 20 declares `eval: tasks file exists with one task per PRD requirement; coverage matrix shows 100% PRD-requirement coverage and zero orphan tasks; every task acceptance is binary; Gate 3 debate manifest closes with Orchestrator sign-off entry; any user-driven recut wrote a record to task-history.json.` There is zero mention of `sprint-bucket`. After 025 ships, a fresh agent running the skill's own binary eval would report PASS on a tasks file that omits the new field entirely. The PRD adds R1/R9 (the field exists; topological-floor invariant holds) and assigns them to AC-1/AC-4/AC-9 verified externally — but the skill's own self-declared `eval:` is what the orchestrator harness runs to decide skill-output validity. R1's outcome is not exercised by the skill that produces it.
findings.evidence: `plugins/specflow/skills/task/SKILL.md` line 20 (current `eval:` text). PRD R1, R9 (new field + invariant). AC-1/AC-4/AC-9 verify the artefact but not via the skill's own `eval:` field. Goal-driven-execution principle: every skill that produces output declares verify steps inline; `eval:` must exercise the output it produces.
findings.proposed_change: Append two binary clauses to the `eval:` field in `task/SKILL.md` so it reads (additions in brackets): `... every task acceptance is binary; [every task entry in {NNN-slug}-tasks.md carries a sprint-bucket: N field with N>=1 — verified by `grep -c '^- \*\*sprint-bucket:\*\*' {NNN-slug}-tasks.md` returning a count equal to the number of tasks listed]; [the topological-floor invariant holds — for every task T_i with sprint-bucket: N, every T_j in T_i.Depends-on has sprint-bucket <= N — verified by a parser pass over the tasks file that emits zero violations]; Gate 3 debate manifest closes with Orchestrator sign-off entry; ...`. Also add a corresponding line to the `## Verify before declaring done` checklist (currently lines 462-471) that cites the same two checks.

findings.title: AC-9's `diff <(grep '^sprint-bucket:' ...)` reproducibility check does not match the actual file format
findings.claim: AC-9 specifies `diff <(grep '^sprint-bucket:' run-1.md) <(grep '^sprint-bucket:' run-2.md)` returns empty. But `task/SKILL.md` Phase B.3 template (lines 174-186) writes per-task fields as markdown bullets: `- **context-budget-estimate:** {int_tokens}`. The new `sprint-bucket` field will follow the same template — the line will start `- **sprint-bucket:**`, not `sprint-bucket:`. The literal regex `^sprint-bucket:` matches zero lines in the synthesised file, so `diff` returns empty *trivially*, regardless of whether buckets actually agreed. A fresh agent running this command on two divergent runs would still see PASS. The check is non-binary: it cannot distinguish a reproducible run from a broken one.
findings.evidence: `task/SKILL.md` lines 174-186 (B.3 per-task entry template uses `- **field:** value` format). PRD AC-9 line 116 (`diff <(grep '^sprint-bucket:' run-1.md) <(grep '^sprint-bucket:' run-2.md)`). Additional edge cases: a task whose `Notes:` field literally contains the string `sprint-bucket:` (e.g. discussing the field) would also leak into the grep output, polluting the diff.
findings.proposed_change:
Rewrite AC-9's verification to a parser-grade check that survives the actual file format. Replace the verify command with a tasks-file-aware extraction: `python3 -c 'import re,sys; s=open(sys.argv[1]).read(); print("
".join(re.findall(r"### (T\d+).*?
(?:.*
)*?- \*\*sprint-bucket:\*\* (\d+)", s)))' {NNN-slug}-tasks.md > run-N.buckets` then `diff run-1.buckets run-2.buckets`. Specify the exact extraction pattern in the AC so a fresh agent reproduces it bit-for-bit. Reject any verify-step that relies on `^sprint-bucket:` matching the live file.

findings.title: AC-13 verifies the *doc lists* phase ordering but does not verify the *implementation runs* in that order
findings.claim: AC-13 (line 128-129) verifies that `task/SKILL.md` Phase D documents the explicit phase ordering (a) per-task budget check, (b) bucket assignment, (c) topological-floor invariant — verbatim listed in that order. But documenting an order is not running an order. A fresh agent reading the doc can confirm the prose but cannot confirm the synthesis pass actually executes the three phases in sequence. R7's intent (`a bucket-assignment run that finds a task with context-budget-estimate exceeding the budget aborts and re-routes through (a) — bucketing never operates on a task list with un-split oversize tasks`) is an *execution-order* invariant, not a *documentation* invariant. AC-13 fails the binary test for execution.
findings.evidence: PRD AC-13 line 128-129. PRD R7 line 74-76 (execution-order requirement). The verify step proposed (`task/SKILL.md` Phase D verify-step list documents the explicit phase ordering`) is satisfied by writing prose in any order to the file as long as a list of three items appears in (a)(b)(c) sequence — it does not exercise the synthesis runtime.
findings.proposed_change: Add an execution-order verify step to AC-13 (or split it into AC-13a documentation + AC-13b execution): construct a fixture PRD with one task whose `context-budget-estimate` deliberately exceeds the configured budget AND has a `Depends on:` edge. Run `specflow:task` against it. Binary check: the synthesis aborts with the 029-R4 split prompt BEFORE writing any `sprint-bucket: N` field on the oversize task. Verify by: (1) confirming the chat output contains the budget-overrun warning string from B.4 step 5; (2) confirming the resulting tasks file has no `sprint-bucket:` line for the oversize task ID. Both grep-able, both binary.

findings.title: AC-12's hand-edit-detection diagnostic is under-specified — fresh agent cannot verify the right tasks named or the right delta surfaced
findings.claim: AC-12 (lines 125-126) says the diagnostic 'names the task ID, the existing value, the recomputed value, and points the user to specflow:scope-change.' This is too loose for a binary verify step. A fresh agent presented with two synthesis runs (one with a hand-edited bucket value) needs to assert: (i) the diagnostic mentions the *specific* task ID that was edited (not 'a task'); (ii) the diagnostic surfaces *both* values (existing AND recomputed) in machine-readable form; (iii) if multiple tasks were hand-edited, all are listed (not just the first); (iv) if zero hand-edits exist, no false-positive diagnostic fires. The PRD names none of these. Two implementations could both 'name the task ID' and disagree on whether they pass.
findings.evidence: PRD AC-12 line 125-126. PRD R10 line 86-88 (enforcement contract). Compare against R9/AC-4 which names the invariant ('topological-floor invariant') as a stable label — AC-12 has no equivalent stable label or message-format anchor.

findings.title: AC-3's worked example exercises the happy path but no AC exercises edge cases — self-loops, cycles, duplicate IDs are silently undefined
findings.claim: AC-3 demonstrates parallelism (T1 + T3 share bucket 1) and the topological floor (T2 → bucket 2). It does NOT exercise: (a) a task whose `Depends on:` lists itself (self-loop) — the heuristic `bucket(T) = 1 + max(bucket(D) for D in T.depends_on)` hangs forever or produces undefined output; (b) a cycle T1 → T2 → T1 — same problem; (c) duplicate task IDs (T2 and T2) — the heuristic's `T_i.id < T_j.id` tie-break collapses; (d) a task whose `Depends on:` references a task that doesn't exist (typo / dangling reference). R2's heuristic must be defined on these inputs OR the synthesis must reject them. Today neither is specified, so two implementations may diverge silently and no AC catches it.
findings.evidence: PRD AC-3 lines 98-99 (worked example, three-task happy path). PRD R2 lines 51-56 (heuristic — recursive definition assumes a DAG with unique IDs, no validation step). No AC for cycle / self-loop / duplicate-ID rejection.
findings.proposed_change: Add AC-14: the bucket-assignment phase rejects malformed task graphs with a deterministic error before any `sprint-bucket: N` is written. Specifically: (i) self-loop (`T.depends_on` contains `T`) → abort with `GRAPH-INVALID: self-loop on {T_id}`; (ii) cycle (any strongly-connected component of size >1) → abort with `GRAPH-INVALID: cycle: {T_id_1} -> {T_id_2} -> ... -> {T_id_1}`; (iii) duplicate task IDs → abort with `GRAPH-INVALID: duplicate task ID {T_id}`; (iv) dangling reference → abort with `GRAPH-INVALID: {T_id}.depends_on references unknown task {T_other}`. Binary verify: construct one fixture per case, run synthesis, grep stderr for the literal `GRAPH-INVALID:` prefix and the matching subtype string.

findings.title: AC-7 and AC-10 use absence-of-text checks — soft verification, not binary exercise
findings.claim: AC-7 ('Verified by absence of any cross-feature bucket-merging logic in task/SKILL.md') and AC-10 ('Verified by absence of those concepts in the file') rely on a fresh agent confirming that *something is not present*. Absence checks are notoriously soft: 'cross-feature bucket-merging logic' has no defined token to grep for; a future implementation could add such logic under a different name and AC-7 still passes. Same for AC-10's 'auto-tuning' and 'DAG visualisation' — neither is defined as a literal string set. The check is semantic, not binary.
findings.evidence: PRD AC-7 line 110-111, AC-10 line 119-120. Goal-driven-execution principle: 'eval that doesn't exercise output' is an anti-pattern; absence-of-vague-concept checks fall under this.
findings.proposed_change: For AC-7: replace the absence check with a positive structural assertion. Run synthesis on two independent fixture features A and B; assert that A's tasks file and B's tasks file are independently valid (each passes AC-4 / AC-6) and that no shared file is written referencing both feature IDs alongside a bucket number. Concretely: `grep -lE '(featureA|featureB).*sprint-bucket' plugins/specflow/skills/` returns no file outside the two feature directories. For AC-10: define a closed token list — `auto-tune`, `auto-detect`, `bucket count`, `DAG`, `visualisation`, `visualization`, `render` — and assert none appear in `task/SKILL.md` outside the explicit Non-goals call-out (which the PRD already documents at lines 34-35). `grep -wE '(auto-tune|auto-detect|DAG|visuali[sz]ation)' plugins/specflow/skills/task/SKILL.md` returns only lines inside an explicit `<!-- non-goal -->` marker block, or zero.
